limitations: Eight source statements have agent-reviewed authored teaching, not whole-chapter or learner/exam certification.
Practical methods/data are illustrative; no experiments or independent examiner calibration were performed.

requirements.judgement: Carbohydrate C/H/O correctly identified; distinction between atoms and glucose units is explicitly assessed.
Protein C/H/O/N identified, optional sulfur qualified and nitrogen-only classification correctly rejected.
Fats/oils C/H/O identified without treating triglycerides as repeating-chain polymers; shared element list is not a unique identity test.
Starch and glycogen described as many joined glucose units with distinct storage contexts; simple sugars not all classed as polymers.
Protein amino-acid chains and folding explained and separately assessed from elemental nitrogen.
Typical triglyceride one glycerol/three fatty acids is accurate and distinguished from protein or carbohydrate chains.
Separate aqueous food extract, heated Benedict’s, precipitate observation and glucose/reducing-sugar specificity limits reviewed; incomplete heating cannot establish a negative.
Separate retained starch portion/slurry and unheated iodine blue-black observation avoid filtering out target starch.
Ready-prepared Biuret or correct alkaline-then-dilute-copper sequence gives purple, without heating; reagents and negative blue distinguished.
Clear ethanol extract transferred to water gives a new white emulsion, not starting solids; no ignition sources/heating and school handling/disposal stated.
Positive/negative controls, equal conditions, contamination and detection limits support original mixed-sample interpretations without invented concentrations.
Catalytic metabolic action, active-site specificity and lower activation barrier explained without energy creation or enzyme intention.
Substrate/product cycle and reusable catalyst explicitly worked; irreversible damage distinguished from consumption in a reaction.
Warming increases initial successful collision frequency while other conditions comparable, not an indefinitely rising rate law.
Excess heat changes folded structure/active-site function; optimum is enzyme/condition-specific rather than a universal temperature.
Recovery assay distinguishes reversible cooling from persistent heat damage with qualified outcomes; censored endpoint evidence alone does not prove mechanism.
Stand-alone sampling/iodine endpoint procedure now complete for Paper1; temperature, pH, starting quantities, mixing and fresh enzyme controlled independently.
Matched-endpoint reciprocal-mean calculations, units, rate ratio and graph axes checked; no mass-product rate is invented.
Fresh portions, exposure time, actual stable temperature, repeated spread, finer peak sampling and right-censored outcomes correctly constrain inference.
pH affects charges/interactions and active-site function; enzyme-specific optimum and possible extreme-pH structural disruption accurately qualified.
Best tested pH is distinguished from exact optimum; original pH repeat rates compare1.8-fold and require closer values, not assumed irreversible damage.
Own-source boldB scope retained onlyPaper2B; buffer/finalpH and constant temperature, volumes, concentration, fresh enzyme and removed-sample indicator method reviewed.
Mean-time60s reciprocal0.0167s⁻¹ and repeat interpretation accurate; reciprocal of mean distinguished from mean of reciprocals.
After50/by60s sampling bounds, detection endpoint, no-enzyme control and not-reached outcomes reviewed; timer precision does not remove interval uncertainty.
